resources.string: Installing the plugin (compiling and testing on this device)…
Plugin installed: %1$s. It is in the Plugins category of effects.
Projects that use this effect keep its values and work again if you reinstall the plugin.
Plugins are effects made by other editors: .aureaplugin files or ISF shaders (.fs). Once installed, they are in the Plugins category of the effects browser.
Plugins run only on the GPU, with no access to your files. Aurea compiles and tests each one on this device before installing it.

1. Make a folder with plugin.json (id, name, parameters) and a .frag shader with the function vec4 aurea_main(vec2 uv).
2. Parameters become names in the shader; aurea_source is the layer image and aurea.time the time.
3. To combine Aurea effects without a shader, use the "stack" kind.
4. Pack it with pack_plugin.py and install it here. An ISF shader (.fs) also works directly.
The full guide, with examples, is in Aurea's docs/plugins.
